### Out of MCPJa

MCPJam refused the call before it reached a provider. For the daily, monthly,
and general codes, the account's own
allowance is spent.\n`provider/mcpjam_limit_insufficient` means the balance is not empty but is below\nwhat the request could cos
t. Which allowance depends on the plan: free accounts\nshare a daily bucket per organization, paid plans spend a monthly allowance

**Next steps**

* **Free plan (owner)** — The limit dialog shows **Compare plans** to upgrade, and **Learn more about
BYOK** to understand how provider keys and MCPJam credits work separately.\n* **Free plan (admin or member)** — The dialog shows
a **Request upgrade** link to email an organization owner.\n* **Paid plan (owner or admin)** — The dialog shows **Buy credits** to
add shared credits to your organization.\n* **Paid plan (member)** — The dialog shows a **Request credits** link to email an orga
nization owner.\n* Add your own API key under **Settings → LLM Providers** for chat (BYOK does not cover Swarm, Evals, or other MC
PJam-billed features).\n* If your organization uses its own keys for all AI features, model tokens are billed by its providers ins

tead; see [Organization AI key policy](#organization-ai-key-policy).

**Swarm and Eval runs**

When credits run out during a S
warm or Eval run, blocked work stops and you receive one credit-exhaustion prompt per run, or one per swarm when a swarm launches
several runs at once. Completed results are preserved. Buying credits does not automatically restart the run — start a new run onc

e credits are available.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Bring-your-own-key covers chat. Swarm persona generation and persona-driver
> turn
s are billed to MCPJam and have no personal BYOK path, so adding a key\n> does not lift this limit for a swarm. An organization th
at uses its own keys\n> for all AI features runs those turns on its default AI model instead, and its\n> providers bill their toke

ns; see
> [Organization AI key policy](#organization-ai-key-policy).
